summary:
The Ilocos Region stands under the national framework of the Philippines.

Bayambang, a municipality in Pangasinan, enforces Municipal Ordinance No. 15, s-2023, which protects lesbians, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer and intersex people in the municipality against discrimination solely on the basis of sexual orientation, gender identity, expression and sex characteristics. The penalty ladder runs from a fine of at least 1,000 pesos or one month's imprisonment for a first offence, to at least 2,000 pesos or between one month and a day and six months for a second, to at least 2,500 pesos or between six months and a day and eight months for a third. A subsequent violation carries one year's imprisonment and a fine of at least 2,500 pesos. Every violator must also complete mandatory human rights education.

Complaints are filed through the barangay Katarungang Pambarangay mechanism established by the Local Government Code, Republic Act 7160. A trans visitor discriminated against inside Bayambang therefore has a local complaint route that does not depend on a national anti-discrimination statute.

The Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Pangasinan adopted Resolution No. 799-2024 at its session of 19 August 2024 in Lingayen, declaring the Bayambang ordinance conformant with the Bill of Rights and Section 16 of Republic Act 7160. The resolution is a provincial-level endorsement of the municipal instrument; it does not extend the ordinance's protections to other municipalities in Pangasinan.

The municipality's official ordinance registry records the instrument as dated 16 October 2023, authored by Coun. Benjamin Francisco S. De Vera, and publishes a certified copy for public view.

The ordinance's reach stops at the municipal boundary. The source inventory contains no region-specific legal instrument, enforcement record or incident for Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur or La Union, so for those provinces the national assessment applies without local modification.
tangentialFactors:
The complaint channel is a general local dispute-resolution mechanism under the Local Government Code rather than a dedicated SOGIESC body: a discrimination complaint enters the same barangay process used for other local disputes.

The provincial resolution is a conformity finding under the Local Government Code's general welfare provision. It creates no provincial anti-discrimination ordinance and no provincial enforcement body, so protection outside Bayambang depends on whether another municipality has adopted its own instrument.

The ordinance reaches discrimination solely on the listed grounds, which sets the boundary of what the local route covers.
localsOnly:
For residents of Bayambang, the ordinance is enforced locally: complaints go through the barangay justice mechanism rather than a national agency, and the municipality, not a national body, is the venue.

Residents found in violation face the fine or imprisonment ladder plus mandatory human rights education, and the provincial board's conformity finding means the ordinance has been reviewed against the Local Government Code at provincial level.
outOfScopeNotes:
A journal article on the bodong customary-justice system, described as adopted and modified by Itneg elders in Abra and Ilocos Sur as an alternative dispute-resolution body operating alongside Philippine courts and police, could not be retrieved: the host returned a 403 anti-bot response and a zero-length extract. No finding is drawn from it, and its bearing on trans visitors in Ilocos Sur is unresolved.

No region-specific legal instrument, enforcement action or incident for Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur or La Union appears in this inventory. Those provinces rest on the national assessment alone.

The inventory does not record any complaint filed, charge brought or penalty imposed under Bayambang Municipal Ordinance No. 15, s-2023, so the ordinance's operation in practice is not sourced.
